summary: This photodecarboxylation reaction uses direct photochemical excitation (no external photocatalyst) to achieve benzylation via triplet sensitization mechanism. The reaction is conducted at 80°C with a 78-minute residence time in an FEP capillary reactor (0.8 mm ID, 5 mL volume) using fluorescent tube irradiation and a mixed solvent system of acetone/pH 7 buffer, dichloromethane, and DMF. The flow setup employs syringe pumps at 0.25 mL/min flow rate to deliver reactants through the photoreactor. Flow chemistry dramatically improved the process by increasing yield from 45% to 77% while maintaining the same 9-hour total reaction time as batch, representing a 6.9× intensification factor. The continuous flow approach eliminated the need for multiple solvent changes required in batch processing and provided better control over reaction conditions with enhanced safety through reduced exposure to hazardous reagents.

summary: This study describes a photocatalyzed aerobic oxidation using 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole as the photocatalyst at 10 mol% loading. The reaction was conducted at 25°C with a 2-minute residence time in acetonitrile solvent using 420 nm LED irradiation. The flow setup employed a fixed-bed reactor (FBR) with 6 mm ID borosilicate glass tubing, 6 mL reactor volume, and 0.2 mL/min flow rate with a back pressure regulator at 1 bar. The flow process achieved 97.2% yield compared to 99% in batch, demonstrating nearly equivalent performance with significantly reduced reaction time from the batch baseline. The flow approach enabled precise control over residence time and continuous processing while maintaining high efficiency for this photocatalytic transformation.

summary: This photocatalyzed radical addition employs 2-benzopyrylium intermediates generated in situ as the photoredox catalyst under 450 nm LED irradiation. The flow process operates in a 1.0 mL photochemical reactor using 1,2-dichloroethane as solvent at room temperature (25°C) with a 2.5 minute residence time and 24.0 mL/min flow rate, achieving 77% yield. In contrast, the batch baseline required elevated temperature (50°C) and 60 minutes reaction time to obtain 76% yield. Flow processing provided a 24-fold intensification in reaction rate while maintaining comparable yield and enabling safer room temperature operation, demonstrating superior scalability for this photoredox transformation.
